title: Plants Get Matter from Air and Water
seo_title: Grade 5 Plant Growth Worksheets: What Plants Need, Air, Water and the Willow Tree
standard_text: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on what plants need to grow (NGSS 5-LS1-1): light, water, air and nutrients, the willow tree experiment, hydroponics and plant investigations. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Plants build their bodies mostly from air and water.
key_sub: Light gives energy. Carbon dioxide from the air and water give the matter. Soil adds only a few nutrients.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants need light, water, air and a few nutrients. But where does the matter that makes a plant bigger come from?

Plants build their bodies mostly from carbon dioxide from the air and water. Using energy from light, they make sugar (photosynthesis), and they use the sugar to build leaves, stems, roots and fruit. Soil gives only small amounts of nutrients.

StartAfter 5 years
Mass of willow tree2 kg74 kg
Mass of dry soil90 kg89.9 kg

In a famous experiment, a willow tree gained more than 70 kg while the soil lost almost nothing. The new matter came from air and water.

Example

A plant gains 120 g while the soil in its pot loses 2 g. Where did most of the 120 g come from?

2 g is tiny compared with 120 g.

The rest came from carbon dioxide and water.

Answer: air and water

Example

Two identical plants get the same water and soil. One is in a sunny window and one is in a dark closet. What is being tested?

Only the light is different.

Answer: whether plants need light

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants “eat” soil. Soil barely loses mass as a plant grows.
  • Thinking sunlight becomes the plant's matter. Light gives energy, not matter.
  • Thinking “plant food” from a store is the plant's food. Plants make their own food (sugar).
  • Changing more than one thing in a plant investigation.

faq.q: Where do plants get the materials to grow?
faq.a: Mostly from carbon dioxide in the air and from water. Soil gives only small amounts of nutrients.

faq.q: Do plants get their food from the soil?
faq.a: No. Plants make their own food (sugar) from carbon dioxide and water using energy from light.

faq.q: What was the willow tree experiment?
faq.a: A willow tree grew in a pot for 5 years with only water added. The tree gained about 74 kg, but the soil lost only a tiny amount, so the tree's mass did not come from the soil.
Yes. In hydroponics, plants grow with their roots in water and a few added nutrients.

items.q: A seed grew into a plant in a pot. The soil lost only about 2 g. Where did most of the plant's added mass come from?
c: carbon dioxide from the air and water
items.e: The plant gained about 99 g but the soil lost only 2 g. Plants build their bodies from carbon dioxide and water.

items.q: Through which part do plants take in carbon dioxide?
items.e: Tiny openings in leaves let carbon dioxide in.

items.q: What do plants need to grow?
c: light, water, air and a few nutrients
items.e: Plants need light for energy, water and carbon dioxide (from air) for matter, and small amounts of nutrients.

items.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air to grow?
items.e: Leaves take in carbon dioxide through tiny openings.

items.q: A farm grows tomatoes with their roots in water and a few nutrients, and no soil at all. The plants grow big and healthy. What does this show?
c: The plants are not really growing.
Plants do not need soil to get the matter they use to grow.
items.e: This is called hydroponics. The plants get matter from air and water and only small amounts of nutrients.
